new_statements.rule_in_words: Word accent falls on the penultimate syllable, described as light; a very few (unspecified) exceptions exist. Vowel length is phonemic (long vowels written aa, ee, ii, oo, uu), so the interaction of length with penultimate accent is not stated.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not mentioned in the retrieved snippets.
new_statements.exceptions: 'With a very few exceptions' - the exceptions are not enumerated in any snippet retrieved; the full page could not be opened.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level ('the penultimate syllable'), from an anthropologist's one-page orthography/phonology appendix, not a linguist's analysis; no examples with marked stress were retrievable. Accent characterized as 'lightly' realized. Statement obtained from scanned snippets returned by the archive.org full-text search API for a lending-restricted scan; overlapping snippets from six separate queries agree word for word, but the printed page itself has not been viewed.
new_statements.identity_note: Ross 1973 describes the Baegu of the northern Malaita interior (East Baegu ward and West Baegu/Fataleka), fieldwork 1966-68; he treats Lau, To'abaita, Baelelea, Baegu and possibly Fataleka as dialects of one North Malaitan language ('Bali'), and the statement is for Baegu proper (baeg1237), not the Fiji koine Wai (Siegel 1986). No sub-dialect is named for the accent statement.

sources.citation: Ross, Harold M. 1973. Baegu: social and ecological organization in Malaita, Solomon Islands (Illinois Studies in Anthropology 8). Urbana: University of Illinois Press.
sources.quote: While speech patterns tend to be fairly rapid, most people's pronunciation is precise, with syllables being clearly enunciated and easily separable. With a very few exceptions, the penultimate syllable is lightly accented.
sources.locator: Appendix A: Baegu Phonology, p. 293 (page per the table of contents and MLA Bibliography 1975 record; the sentence immediately precedes the 'Typewritten symbol / Phonetic symbol' table that opens the appendix)
sources.note: The only located first-hand phonology statement for Baegu; the full page is needed to read the 'very few exceptions', the symbol table (vowel length marking) and any accent-marked examples in the glossary. archive.org holds a lending copy (baegusocialecolo0000ross) that can be borrowed by a logged-in user; also in print at university libraries.

sources.citation: Siegel, Jeff. 1986. Wai: a Malaitan language in Fiji. In P. Geraghty, L. Carrington & S.A. Wurm (eds), FOCAL II: Papers from the Fourth International Conference on Austronesian Linguistics, 435-463. Pacific Linguistics C-94. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Sec. 3.2 'Wai phonology' (pp. 447-448) gives segments and phonemic vowel length only; grep of the full text for stress/accent/penult finds nothing except an informant remark that Wai 'rhythm and intonation sound like Lau' (p. 444). Baegu figures only as one of the North Malaitan input dialects (Table 2-1, p. 439; informants Peter Sukuomea and Timothy Beliga, n. 15). Describes Wai (Fiji koine), not Baegu.
Bibliographic only: Tryon & Hackman 1983 (overview), Siegel 1986 (overview), Ross 1973 (minimal); no grammar, sketch or phonology listed (n_glottolog_desc_refs = 0).

sources.citation: Na Alangaia Falu 'ana Baea 'i Baegu: Baegu New Testament. SITAG / Wycliffe Bible Translators, 2016 (eBible id BVDWBT, bvd).
sources.note: Scripture text in a practical orthography (glottal stop written with apostrophe); no linguistic front matter; confirms SITAG translation work in Baegu but no phonology statement.

sources.citation: Tryon, Darrell T. & B.D. Hackman. 1983. Solomon Islands languages: an internal classification. Pacific Linguistics C-72. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Baegu ('Baeguu', 'Mbaengguu') is a North Malaitan wordlist in the lexicostatistical tables; the only 'stress' hits are 'It is stressed however...' (p. 51 prose) and 'in unstressed syllables' footnotes in the POc reflex tables for other languages; no prosodic statement for Baegu or any language.
No phonology section; classification and speaker numbers only.
